I haven't confirmed any specs or prices from this session, so treat the points below as starting places and check them.

**What matters for pool or beach**
- **Rating:** Look for IP67 or higher. That covers dust and sand as well as water. IPX7 alone covers water but not sand.
- **Floating:** This is useful at the pool, because a speaker that sinks is easy to lose.
- **Battery:** Aim for 12 hours or more, so it lasts a full day outside.
- **Loudness:** Open air swallows sound, so a mid-size speaker usually beats a tiny one.

**Models to look at**
- **JBL Xtreme 5:** It appeared on the RTINGS page's "Popular" list. It's a larger, louder speaker for beach days. I haven't confirmed its specs or price. Check [RTINGS' waterproof speaker list](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth).
- **Ultimate Ears MEGABOOM 4:** It also appeared in that RTINGS sidebar. UE's Boom line has long been built to float. I haven't confirmed the specs for this model.
- **soundcore Boom 2 Plus:** This is an outdoor speaker. A deal-site listing says it's $249.99 and drops to about $200 with code AFSC20, tested in Soundcore's cart on 2026-10-22. I couldn't verify that, so confirm the price at checkout. I also couldn't verify its waterproof rating or battery life. [Deal link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**My suggestion**
Compare the JBL Xtreme 5 and the UE MEGABOOM 4 first, since they're the two the RTINGS page surfaced. Check each one's IP rating, floating, and battery life on the product page before you buy. If you tell me your budget and whether you want a small or a party-loud speaker, I can narrow it down.

Sources: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/lab/V7/soundcore-boom-2-plus)
